collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DEPARTURES AND EXILE (DEP-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Leaving and being left: moving huts, short journeys, visitors going home, goodbyes done well and badly, homesickness, and the rare person who sails away for good. Choosing to leave is never a rejection of one's people, and choosing to stay is never a failure.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult)

collection.description: A villager moving huts cannot part with an old cracked cooking pot: keep it, or leave it for the next person.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (name1) is moving huts tomorrow, and everything is packed except one cooking pot. It's old. It has a crack down one side that leaks if you fill it past halfway. It has made, (name1) estimates, about a thousand stews. There's a perfectly good newer pot already packed. (name1) is sitting on the floor holding the old one.

choices.label: Leave It for the Next Person

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The old pot goes too. In the new hut it doesn't get used for cooking anymore. It sits on a shelf, holding nothing in particular, and every now and then (name1) looks at it and thinks of a thousand stews. That seems like a fine job for an old pot.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (name1) leaves it by the hearth, cleaned and full of fresh water, for whoever lives here next. A few weeks later (he/she) passes the old hut and smells stew cooking. (He/she) is almost certain it's in the old pot. (He/she) is right. It leaks a little. The new family doesn't mind.
